newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy official sees '98 budget of 25 trln lire cuts.
newsitem.headline: Italy official sees '98 budget of 25 trln lire cuts.

text.p: Italy needs a deficit-cutting budget of around 25 trillion lire for 1998 to keep meet conditions for membership of Europe's planned single currency, treasury and budget ministry undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said on Friday.
He told Reuters in a telephone interview that without such deficit cuts, the ratio between the deficit and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1998 would be "a little over four percent".

The European Union's Maastricht Treaty lays down a deficit-GDP ratio of three percent for countries which aim to qualify for planned economic and monetary union (EMU), scheduled for launch on January 1, 1999.
"The tendential (deficit-GDP ratio) is running out at a little over four percent," Macciotta said.
"Since the objective is to be below three percent, the budget has to be around 1.2 (percentage) points, equivalent to around 25 trillion," Macciotta said.
European Union finance ministers, in a strongly worded document released earlier this week, urged Italy to aim for a deficit/GDP ratio below the three percent threshold established for EMU aspirants.
